page.title: VMs & containers
page.subtitle: VMs and containers of Proxmox VE 8.4 or newer, backed up through the official backup interface of Proxmox VE. Only changed data leaves the node.
page.limits: Not possible in this release: backing up VM templates, live restore, restoring privileged containers, restoring single files from VMs.
page.loadError: The data could not be loaded.

connect.title: Connect Proxmox VE
connect.description: One command per node, run as root. It sets up the user restow@pve, its roles and the restore pool, creates the node's own API token, picks the fleecing storage and connects the node. Nothing to type: the API token stays on the node.
connect.existingToggle: Use an existing PVE API token instead
connect.existingHint: Only needed if your rules call for a token you created yourself. It needs privilege separation off and the roles from the documentation; the installer checks its privileges before it changes anything.
connect.tokenIdUnexpected: {appName} expects the user restow@pve. Another user works if it has the same roles.
connect.secretInvalid: The secret Proxmox VE showed once when the token was created (a UUID).
connect.existingSecurity: {appName} stores the token encrypted, hands it to the node once while it connects and then deletes it, at the latest when the command expires.
connect.runHint: Run as root on the node. Works for one node until {expires}.
connect.usesToken: This command uses the API token {tokenId} entered here. If that token is gone or lacks privileges, create a new command without it.
connect.anotherHint: Every node needs its own command. Connect the nodes one after another; the first one adds the storage to the cluster.

nodes.title: Nodes

nodes.revokeDescription: The node can no longer back up or restore. Existing restore points are kept.

hostFiles.title: The Proxmox host itself is not backed up here
hostFiles.body: restow-pve backs up the VMs and containers of a node, not the node. For the host's own files, such as /etc/pve and the network and storage configuration, install the {appName} agent on the host and put it into a server job.

jobs.bootTestHint: Proves that a restore point boots: the node restores it to a temporary guest with its network cut, starts it, waits for the QEMU Guest Agent and deletes the guest again. Needs memory and space on the node.

restore.title: Restore as a new guest
restore.description: The restore point is created as a new guest in the pool restow-restore. The original stays as it is.
restore.queued: Restore requested. The node starts it at its next check-in, usually within a minute.
restore.privileged: Proxmox VE cannot restore privileged containers from a backup interface.

result.green: The restore check of the newest restore point confirmed every block it read.
result.red: The restore check of the newest restore point failed: blocks did not match or could not be read.
result.unverified: A restore point exists but has not been checked yet.
result.noBackup: Nothing to check until the first backup has finished.
result.noBackupOverdue: No backup within 24 hours after the guest was put into a backup job.
result.bootGreen: The newest restore point booted in its boot test: the guest agent answered.
result.bootYellow: The newest restore point started in its boot test, but its guest agent did not answer: no proof the system works.
result.bootRed: The newest restore point did not boot in its boot test.

selfBackup.title: This guest runs {appName} itself
selfBackup.short: Runs {appName} itself: not backed up until you confirm.
selfBackup.confirmedShort: Runs {appName} itself: backing it up was confirmed.
selfBackup.confirmedLong: An administrator confirmed backing it up with {appName} anyway.

reason.detected: {appName} found it: its SMBIOS UUID is the one of the machine {appName} runs on.
reason.flagged: An administrator marked it as the {appName} server.

selfBackup.risk: Backing up the VM that runs {appName} with {appName} itself can deadlock: the backup freezes or snapshots the server that receives the backup, and restoring it needs the very server that is being restored.
selfBackup.recommendation: Back this VM up with Proxmox VE's own backup (vzdump) to another storage, and keep {appName}'s database dumps (docs/DATABASE.md). Confirm only if you accept the risk.
selfBackup.confirmInJob: I understand the risk and want this VM backed up by this job anyway.
selfBackup.flagHint: Mark the guest {appName} runs in when {appName} cannot find it itself (for example {appName} in a container). It is then not backed up until an administrator confirms it.

settings.title: Proxmox VE
settings.description: How the restore points of VMs and containers are checked.
settings.verifyAfterBackup: Check every new restore point right after the backup
settings.verifyAfterBackupHint: A new restore point is read back within a few minutes of its backup (a sample of its blocks, a container: a restic check of a subset), a bounded number per pass. The weekly check of every guest stays either way. Off: new restore points wait for the weekly check.
